History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
Adult male with 3-day history of watery diarrhea, left-sided crampy lower abdominal pain, transient vomiting, and mild subjective fever—most consistent with acute gastroenteritis likely related to recent takeaway food.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Watery, loose stools for 3 days.  
• Frequency: 6–7 bowel movements/day.  
• Abdominal pain: Cramp-like, intermittent, left lower abdomen; non-radiating.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Initial vomiting on day 1, now resolved.  
  – Subjective fever at onset; none currently.  
  – Weakness/shakiness.  
  – Loss of appetite; tolerating fluids (soups, smoothies).  
• Denies: Hematochezia, hematemesis, persistent fever, night sweats, other GI or systemic complaints.  
• Possible trigger: Chinese restaurant takeaway 4 days ago; one child vomited only.  
• Symptom impact: Needs proximity to toilet; difficult to work but has continued working.  
• Review of systems otherwise negative as per conversation.

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – well controlled with inhaler; no recent exacerbations.

Medications:
• Asthma inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.
Allergies:
• Not discussed – missing.

Social History:
• Lives with wife and two children.  
• Occupation: Accountant.  
• Tobacco: Never smoker.  
• Alcohol: Denies use.  
• No recreational drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed (no data).

Physical Examination:
• Not performed during teleconsult; no vitals provided.

Investigations:
• None to date.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral vs. food-borne bacterial)  
  – Conservative management recommended.  
  – Hydration: Encourage oral fluids; oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte) from pharmacy.  
  – Diet: Light foods as tolerated.  
  – Symptomatic relief: Paracetamol 1 g (two 500 mg tablets) up to q6h PRN for pain/fever.  
  – Activity: Advise 2–3 days off work for rest and to reduce spread.  
  – Warning signs: Worsening pain, persistent fever, blood in stool/vomit, inability to keep fluids down, symptoms >3–4 days.  
  – Follow-up: Re-evaluation if no improvement in 3–4 days; consider stool culture and further work-up if persistent.

General Plan items:
• Provide written hydration and dietary advice.  
• Reinforce hand hygiene to protect family members.  
• Arrange review appointment or telephone follow-up if required.
